items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 11.3.46 at source lines 1636-1646: squaring of rationals extends to a unique function on the Cauchy reals with the explicit Lipschitz bound |u^2 - v^2| <= 2 n |u - v| on [-n,n]. The author's proof (source lines 1648-1680) assembles four separate inputs rather than computing directly: the archimedean property makes the bounded-interval cover surjective onto RC (lines 1649-1658), the retained extension theorem turns squaring on each bounded rational interval, which is Lipschitz with constant 2n, into a map on that interval (lines 1658-1668), compatibility of these extensions on overlaps is deduced from continuity via the retained continuity lemma (lines 1668-1671), and uniqueness is obtained by factoring through the surjection using the retained factorisation result (lines 1671-1679). The statement is a single existence-and-uniqueness assertion with an estimate, and records none of the four steps.
